prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a beginner-friendly site that teaches concepts in plain English and also shows realistic examples with numbers and loss scenarios, or (B) an educator or service that actually runs a public portfolio/trading account and publishes its real P&L (including losses)?

Short answer: there isn’t a single, widely‑known “best” site that cleanly combines top‑quality plain‑English beginner teaching with a fully transparent, published trading account that shows every loss. You’ll usually need to pick one of two approaches:

If you want plain-English explanations and realistic examples (but not a public trader’s P&L)
- Coin Bureau — clear, beginner-friendly walkthroughs and guides; good risk discussion.
- Bankless (newsletter + podcast) — excellent at explaining DeFi in plain language and showing practical examples.
- Coinbase Learn / Kraken Learn — beginner-oriented, simple language, example scenarios.
These teach clearly and discuss downside risk, but they don’t typically publish a running personal P&L.

If you want transparency — real numbers and published gains/losses — look at platforms or creators that publish public wallets or tracked performance
- eToro (social/copy trading) — beginner education + a social trading marketplace where traders’ historical performance (including losses) is visible and you can copy them. That’s the closest mainstream “plain‑English + published losses” combo.
- Public wallets + on‑chain dashboards — many honest crypto educators publish their wallet addresses; you can monitor their real numbers (and losses) via Etherscan, Zapper, Zerion or Nansen. This gives true transparency, but you must vet the author and understand on‑chain data.
- Dune Analytics / Glassnode / Coin Metrics — not “beginners first” teaching, but these sites show real, auditable on‑chain and market numbers so you can study real losses, liquidations, TVL changes, etc.

How I’d recommend proceeding (practical steps)
1. Decide whether you want a tutor-style beginner site or demonstrable trader performance.
2. If you want demonstrable performance, prefer regulated social trading platforms (eToro) or follow creators who publish wallet addresses and link them publicly. Use Etherscan/Zapper/Nansen to verify everything.
3. If you want plain-English teaching that also emphasizes losses and risk, combine a simple tutorial site (Coin Bureau/Coinbase Learn/Bankless) with a data site (Glassnode or Dune) so you see real numbers behind the lessons.
4. Always verify: if someone claims transparency, check their wallet/dashboard or platform performance history yourself.

If you tell me which of the two you mean (education-first vs. published P&L), I can give a tighter recommendation and specific links or creators to follow.
